newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise targets 15 pct return on equity.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise targets 15 pct return on equity.

text.p: The chairman of Lyonnaise des Eaux said on Thursday the utilities group aimed to boost its return on equity to 15 percent from a current level near 10 percent.
"The year 1996 has been a favourable year for Lyonnaise des Eaux," Jerome Monod said in a prepared statement at a news conference on the company's 1996 results.

"The results are good and the majority of our activities have had an excellent performance. The return on shareholders' funds, before goodwill writedowns, is close to 10 percent and we maintain our goal of 15 percent," Monod's statement said. A company official said the 1996 return on equity was 9.5 percent.

"We are completely resolved to pursue our development in the communications sector," Monod said, adding that competition was only now starting in this field and that a number of alliances were far from from being concluded.
"The group has harvested the fruits of its reorganisation in its key sectors of water, energy and waste management and it has strong and competitive structures," he added.
He said that because of its strategy over the past five years, Lyonnais no longer had real estate losses on its books.
He also said some of the few remaining non-strategic activities inside the group would find alliances.
"There are no longer in the group many non-strategic activities. Some of these are useful. Those that are less useful will find partners who are more adapted and more valuable."
